name: PRAJNESH GUNNESWARAN
bio:
Career Overview: Playing Style: A left-handed player with a powerful forehand and aggressive baseline game, strong on hard courts.
Career-High ATP Singles Ranking: #75 (April 22, 2019), Career-High ATP Doubles Ranking: #149 (January 13, 2020).
Best Grand Slam Singles Performance: Reached the first round of all four Grand Slams in 2019 (Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, US Open).
Notable Achievements: Biggest Singles Win: Defeated World No. 18 Nikoloz Basilashvili at the 2019 Indian Wells Masters. ATP Challenger Titles: Won two Challenger singles titles (2018 Anning, 2018 Bengaluru) and one doubles title. ITF Success: Secured 8 ITF Futures singles titles and 1 doubles title. Asian Games: Won a bronze medal in men’s singles at the 2018 Jakarta Asian Games. Davis Cup & National Representation: Represented India in Davis Cup ties from 2017 to 2023, delivering key singles wins.
Other Highlights: Broke into the Top 100 in 2019 after overcoming knee injuries earlier in his career. Retired in November 2024 after a 14-year pro career, citing wrist issues and a desire to move on.
Prajnesh was a late bloomer who became one of India’s top singles players, leaving a legacy of resilience and achievement. 🎾🇮🇳
